On the FedISIC benchmark, PAFP attains the highest unweighted balanced accuracy while reducing inter-client performance variance roughly six-fold relative to the strongest baseline, yielding accuracy and cross-client equity jointly. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/Alexandre-Leclercq/PAFP.
items.title_ko: 혼합 왜곡 환경에서 의료 영상 분류를 위한 연합 전이 학습
items.summary_ko: 의료 영상 분야의 딥러닝은 데이터 희소성 및 환자 데이터 중앙화의 어려움으로 제약을 받습니다. 연합 학습(FL)은 데이터를 로컬에 유지하여 이러한 문제를 해결하지만, 분산된 특성상 강력한 통계적 이질성에 노출됩니다. 이 연구는 기능, 레이블, 개념 및 수량 이동을 결합한 혼합 왜곡을 보이는 의료 데이터에 대한 개인화된 FL을 통해 이러한 이질성을 완화하는 방법을 다룹니다.
items.why_ko: 의료 영상 분야에서 데이터 부족 및 개인 정보 보호 문제를 해결하면서도 모델 성능을 유지하는 방법을 제시하여, 분산된 환경에서의 의료 AI 발전에 기여합니다.

items.title: Whose Effect Is It? How Objectives Inflate Learned Subspace Interventions
items.body: Interpretability often locates concepts by copying part of a language model's state from one input into another (activation patching). A larger output change counts as stronger evidence that this part carries the concept. Methods that learn which part to copy often change the output more than the whole state does. By that reading, learned parts isolate the concept more cleanly. Yet the whole contains the part. So whose effect is this excess, the network's or the method's? Copying the whole state learns nothing, so it shows what the network produces. We prove that, to first order, the effects of orthogonal parts add up to that of the whole. A part therefore exceeds the whole exactly when the rest moves the output back, which does not require isolating the concept more cleanly. Objectives that reward a larger effect select such parts. Distributed alignment search with cross-entropy, for example, exceeds the whole-state copy just before the output on almost all tasks, and inside the network at most sites. In both, changing only its objective to target what the network produces removes most of the excess. It therefore comes largely from the objective, so a larger learned effect alone is not stronger evidence.
items.title_ko: 누구의 효과인가? 객관이 학습된 부분 공간 개입을 부풀리는 방식
items.summary_ko: 해석 가능성 연구는 언어 모델의 상태 일부를 복사하는 활성화 패치(activation patching)를 통해 개념을 파악합니다. 더 큰 출력 변화는 해당 부분이 개념을 더 강력하게 전달한다는 증거로 간주됩니다. 그러나 어떤 부분을 복사할지 학습하는 방법은 때때로 전체 상태보다 더 큰 출력 변화를 일으키는데, 이 연구는 이러한 '초과 효과'가 네트워크의 것인지 방법론의 것인지 의문을 제기합니다.
items.why_ko: 언어 모델 해석 가능성 연구 방법론의 한계를 지적하고, 모델의 내부 작동 방식을 더 정확하게 이해하기 위한 비판적 관점을 제공합니다.

items.title: Comparing model representations and fitting methods for port-Hamiltonian system identification
items.body: Port-Hamiltonian models describe physical systems by separating stored energy, dissipation and external inputs. Learning such models from data requires a choice of representation and fitting method. We compare using neural networks, analytic expressions and combinations of the two for representing the different components of the port-Hamiltonian system, and compare fitting the models with gradient-based optimisation or sparse regression. Testing on simulations of mechanical and electrical systems, with and without added noise, we present prediction accuracy and computational cost of the different approaches.

items.title: DRAP: Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity for Continual Learning in Physical AI
items.body: Continual learning in physical AI differs from conventional continual learning because small per-step policy errors can accumulate over a trajectory. Each deviation may move the agent outside the training distribution, increase subsequent prediction errors, and ultimately cause closed-loop task failure. This work introduces Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity (DRAP), a replay-free method that estimates the historical importance of adaptable model tensors from sample-level action gradients weighted by local trajectory-amplification risk. A ridge-regularized local linear model is fitted to expert state-action transitions, and the largest singular value of its state-transition matrix provides a policy-independent, Lyapunov-inspired estimate of one-step perturbation amplification. After each task, risk-weighted squared gradients are accumulated in a tensor-level importance memory. During subsequent tasks, DRAP uses normalized cumulative importance to scale the effective AdamW learning rate of each tensor, immediately reducing the plasticity of components that supported previous behavior at dynamically sensitive trajectory points. We instantiate DRAP on a fixed KappaTune-selected subnetwork of OpenVLA and evaluate replay-free sequential adaptation across the LIBERO Spatial, Object, and Goal suites. Compared with standard AdamW fine-tuning and EWC, the results show substantially improved retention of previously learned behaviors while preserving strong new-suite acquisition.
items.title_ko: DRAP: 물리 AI의 지속 학습을 위한 동적-위험 적응형 유연성
items.summary_ko: 물리 AI의 지속 학습은 일반적인 지속 학습과 달리, 스텝당 작은 정책 오류도 궤적에 걸쳐 누적될 수 있습니다. 이 연구는 리플레이 없는(replay-free) DRAP (Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity) 방법을 소개하며, 이는 샘플 수준의 액션 그래디언트를 통해 적응 가능한 모델 텐서의 과거 중요도를 추정하고 동적 위험을 고려하여 모델의 유연성을 조절합니다.
items.why_ko: 실제 환경에서 로봇과 같은 물리 AI 에이전트가 새로운 작업을 지속적으로 학습하면서도 안정적인 성능을 유지할 수 있도록 하는 중요한 방법을 제시합니다.

items.title: RGB Photo Enhancement with Deep Learning on Smartphone GPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report
items.body: On-device RGB photo enhancement is a popular task that is needed for quality improvement of photos captured with mobile devices as well as for retouching of images acquired through other sources. This creates a need for efficient deep learning models for this problem that are not only performant but can also be deployed on constrained mobile hardware. In this Mobile AI challenge, we address this problem and propose participants to design fast solutions that can perform comprehensive enhancement of RGB photos while running on popular smartphone GPUs from Qualcomm and Arm. For this, the participants were provided with a large-scale DPED dataset consisting of RGB image pairs captured with an old iPhone 3GS smartphone and a professional Canon 70D DSLR camera. The runtime of all models was evaluated on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 and Dimensity 9500 chipsets with the Adreno and Mali GPUs, respectively. Top solutions proposed in this challenge are able to enhance Full HD resolution RGB images on both platforms under 300 milliseconds. A comprehensive description of the models developed in the challenge is provided in this paper.
items.title_ko: 스마트폰 GPU에서의 RGB 사진 개선: Mobile AI 2026 챌린지 보고서
items.summary_ko: 모바일 기기로 촬영한 사진의 품질 향상 및 보정을 위한 온디바이스(on-device) RGB 사진 개선은 인기 있는 작업입니다. 이 Mobile AI 챌린지에서는 성능이 우수할 뿐만 아니라 제한된 모바일 하드웨어에서도 배포 가능한 효율적인 딥러닝 모델 설계를 참가자들에게 제안했습니다. 이 보고서는 챌린지의 목표와 결과를 다룹니다.
items.why_ko: 모바일 기기에서 딥러닝 모델의 효율적인 배포와 성능 최적화는 실제 사용자 경험에 큰 영향을 미치므로, 온디바이스 AI 개발자들에게 중요한 동향입니다.

items.title: Finite Spectral Depth Controls Gaussian Entrance Rank and Avoidance of the First Gradient-Flow Saddle
items.body: Matrix factorization provides a simple model for studying the training dynamics of neural networks. Recent studies of gradient flow under small initialization have analyzed how trajectories escape from a neighborhood of the origin and approach their first nonzero stationary point. In this paper, we study continuous-time dynamics that applies a finite number of Newton-Schulz iterations to the normalized matrix gradient (Muon). We show that the number of Newton-Schulz steps can change the rank selected during the early stages of training and allow the resulting trajectory to bypass the first nonzero stationary point approached by gradient flow. Under an additional residual-inertia condition, we prove that bypass occurs for all sufficiently large finite Newton-Schulz depths and provide an explicit sufficient threshold. We also construct an example in which the bypass threshold is four.
items.title_ko: 유한 스펙트럼 깊이가 가우시안 진입 랭크 및 첫 번째 경사 흐름 안장점 회피를 제어한다
items.summary_ko: 행렬 분해는 신경망 학습 역학을 연구하기 위한 간단한 모델을 제공합니다. 이 연구는 정규화된 행렬 그래디언트에 유한한 수의 Newton-Schulz 반복을 적용하는 연속 시간 역학을 연구하며, Newton-Schulz 스텝 수가 랭크 선택을 변경할 수 있음을 보여줍니다.
items.why_ko: 신경망 학습 과정의 이론적 이해를 돕고, 최적화 방법론 개발에 기여할 수 있는 연구입니다.

items.title: Rethinking GA2Ms: performance and out-of-distribution generalisation
items.body: Generalised Additive Models (GAMs) are a cornerstone of interpretable machine learning, offering transparent predictions through structured additive decompositions. Despite advances from classical GAMs to modern neural and spline-based variants, two notable gaps remain. First, comprehensive benchmarking of spline-based GAMs on large-scale tabular learning tasks, the dominant modality in applied settings, is lacking. Second, their robustness under distribution shift, a setting where structured inductive biases should confer advantages, remains unexplored. We propose a multi-resolution, higher-order Composite Generalised Additive Model (CoGA2M) and evaluate it on the TALENT benchmark suite. CoGA2M ranks in the top third across all baselines (29 for regression, 32 for classification), establishing competitive performance with state-of-the-art tabular methods. We further extend TALENT with out-of-distribution (OOD) splits exhibiting train-test distributional shift and benchmark CoGA2M against LightGBM, a consistently top-performing model on TALENT. Under distribution shift, CoGA2M outperforms LightGBM, demonstrating a clear structural advantage. Our results position spline-based GAMs as strong contenders for tabular prediction and reveal a previously unrecognised benefit of additive structure in the OOD regime.
items.title_ko: GA2M 재고: 성능 및 분포 외(OOD) 일반화
items.summary_ko: 일반화된 가법 모델(GAM)은 해석 가능한 머신러닝의 중요한 기반으로, 구조화된 가법 분해를 통해 투명한 예측을 제공합니다. 이 연구는 스플라인 기반 GAM의 대규모 테이블형 학습 작업에서의 포괄적인 벤치마킹이 부족하다는 점과, 분포 변화 환경에서의 견고성 부족 문제를 지적하며 이를 재고합니다.
items.why_ko: 해석 가능한 머신러닝 모델의 성능과 실제 환경에서의 견고성에 대한 이해를 심화시켜, 모델 선택 및 적용에 대한 중요한 통찰을 제공합니다.

items.title: datasette-apps 0.3a0
items.body:
Release: datasette-apps 0.3a0

Datasette Apps adds support for hosting and editing custom HTML applications inside of Datasette.

These can be created by hand, but it's easier to create them using LLMs via Datasette Agent. This release improves that integration:

Apps can now be tagged in Datasette Agent chat messages by typing #, which autocompletes from the apps the user has permission to view.

New app_add_stored_queries() and app_remove_stored_queries() tools let the agent manage which stored queries an app is allowed to call. Granting a write query requires approval from the user first.

app_create() now checks that each requested stored query exists and that the user can view it, and asks the user to approve any write queries before the app is created.

The "View app" buttons shown by the agent tools, and the links on # app references, now open the app full screen in the Datasette Agent panel.

Tags: datasette, datasette-agent, datasette-apps
items.title_ko: datasette-apps 0.3a0 릴리스
items.summary_ko: Datasette-Apps 0.3a0 버전이 릴리스되었으며, Datasette 내에서 사용자 정의 HTML 애플리케이션을 호스팅하고 편집하는 기능을 추가합니다. 특히 Datasette Agent와의 통합이 개선되어 에이전트가 채팅 메시지에서 앱을 태그하고, 앱에 저장된 쿼리를 관리하는 등의 작업을 수행할 수 있게 되었습니다.
items.why_ko: Datasette 사용자, 특히 LLM 기반 에이전트를 활용하여 데이터 기반 애플리케이션을 만들고 관리하려는 개발자들에게 유용한 새로운 기능과 개선 사항을 제공합니다.

items.title: datasette-agent 0.5a0
items.body:
Release: datasette-agent 0.5a0

This is a significant release of Datasette Agent. The most notable new feature is called the panel - it lets the agent chat open and then sit next to pages from Datasette, for example a table or query page.

When combined with datasette-apps this means you can prompt a database-backed app into existence and then modify it from the chat that sits next to that app.

You can try it by signing in with your GitHub account to agent.datasette.io.

Tags: projects, datasette, datasette-agent
items.body_ko:
릴리스: datasette-agent 0.5a0

이것은 Datasette Agent의 중요한 릴리스입니다. 가장 눈에 띄는 새로운 기능은 패널이라고 불리는 것으로, 에이전트 채팅을 열고 Datasette의 페이지(예: 테이블 또는 쿼리 페이지) 옆에 둘 수 있습니다.

datasette-apps와 결합하면 데이터베이스 기반 앱을 프롬프트하여 생성한 다음, 해당 앱 옆에 있는 채팅에서 수정할 수 있습니다.

GitHub 계정으로 agent.datasette.io에 로그인하여 사용해 볼 수 있습니다.

태그: projects, datasette, datasette-agent
items.title_ko: datasette-agent 0.5a0 릴리스: 채팅 패널 기능 추가
items.summary_ko: Datasette Agent의 0.5a0 버전이 대폭 업데이트되었습니다. 가장 주목할 만한 새로운 기능은 '패널(panel)'로, 에이전트 채팅이 Datasette 페이지(예: 테이블 또는 쿼리 페이지) 옆에 열려 함께 작동할 수 있습니다. 이 기능은 datasette-apps와 결합하여 데이터베이스 기반 앱을 프롬프트로 생성하고 채팅을 통해 수정할 수 있도록 해줍니다.
items.why_ko: Datasette와 LLM 기반 에이전트의 통합을 심화하여, 개발자가 데이터베이스 기반 애플리케이션을 보다 직관적이고 효율적으로 구축하고 상호작용할 수 있는 강력한 도구를 제공합니다.

items.title: How big is the open model economy today?
items.body:
My longest running agent testbed has been building the Interconnects Dashboard — an aggregator of all of the best data on open model adoption and performance from across the web. This dashboard is freely available and becoming quite useful. Still, all the measurements we have on open model adoption are incredibly imprecise. We have noisy platform metrics, marketing-related metrics from startups, and imperfect public evaluations. It takes an informed eye to figure out where things are going. These research notes are my current best approximations of where we stand.
As with most things on Interconnects, our goal is to build well more value than we capture, so the data on the dashboard will remain free for the foreseeable future. These notes will be more raw than many of my articles, a place for sharing what I’m mulling over but don’t have complete evidence for (yet). They will be primarily paid, enabling me to speak more freely. If you work in AI policy or policy-facing research, please reach out to us and we can likely get discounted or free access.
The primary question I wanted to address today is: What is the market for open model inference? Is it growing? Is it a rounding error relative to OpenAI/Anthropic?
Share
I’ve been building the best measurements I can here, primarily using the open model inference startups Baseten, Fireworks, and Together AI as the bellwethers here (along with the open model share of OpenRouter’s token volume, which they thankfully report in their API). The hyperscalers also likely have a major footprint here, e.g. Amazon Bedrock and Azure’s model garden, but I haven’t seen them break down usage by model category. The startups’ fates are much more directly correlated with the success of open model inference as a category.
For the latest data, we can start with a slide from my talk on the open model economy (recording here). These are the public disclosures from the open model startups on their token volume, over time, log-scale.

This shows near-exponential growth, before the uptick that would follow GLM 5.2’s step change in open agents. For example, Fireworks announced at their first company conference this week that they’re serving more than 40T tokens per day to customers’ customized models. This is just one slice of their inference, a vertical that they said grew over 2x from this summer, so I would expect their total number this fall to be well above 100T tokens when we get the next update.
My first instinct with these numbers has been to ground them versus any closed model or hyperscale company we can, at least in terms of token volume. Thankfully, Google releases token volumes for the entire platform and API usage in their earnings reports. We can overlay those two numbers on top of the open model inference platforms, with the resulting plot below:

items.title: [AINews] Behind Latent Space: Kill My SaaS, Jev & AI in 2026 | AIEi Shanghai
items.body:
There’s a lot of dispute to yesterday’s title story on “Weight Space Programming” — and we agree that some of the claims are presented in overly favorable light and overall took away from the impact of the paper’s more substantial discoveries. However it is still a big wakeup moment and has had multiple independent replications by now that it is not worth either doing some kind of retraction or a followup title story saying it was bogus.

Instead today we’re featuring AI Engineer Shanghai and also sharing an exclusive interview on the history of Latent Space!

AI News for 11/02/2026-11/03/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews' website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space. You can opt in/out of email frequencies!

AI Twitter Recap

Weight-Space Programming: Frontier Models Reading and Writing Neural Network Weights

Core claim and replications: Several groups report that frontier LLMs can generate or edit small networks' weights directly, without gradient training or tools.
Cross-generation replication: Alex Krentsel's replication of MIT's experiment found a sharp capability jump across model generations; the latest models generated Breakout networks scoring up to 22× an RL-trained baseline (summary).

Hugging Face reproduction: Hugging Face reproduced the paper with ML Intern, its open-source AI-research harness, and released the model and a demo (NielsRogge).

Hand-written classifier: A user had Fable hand-write a 100K-parameter network that classifies real versus fake legal citations, reportedly outperforming a trained version (jacsebl). Legora's CTO highlighted the result (mstockton).

Astra's Qwen edit, reconstructed: GPT-6 Astra edited 131,072 weights in Qwen3.5-0.8B without backprop, raising MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%. A Zhihu reconstruction from the logs shows the gain is narrower than the headline (ZhihuFrontier):
Failure mode: 576 of 579 repaired answers had originally hit the 32K-token limit because of looping.

Method: Astra derived a "repetition direction" from contrastive looping/productive contexts, located it mainly in the MLPs of layers 15 and 19, and subtracted 6× the projection from the top 64 aligned neurons per layer.

Held-out result: Accuracy rose from 10.6% to 60.4% on 1,152 held-out problems. Most of the gain is existing reasoning that can now finish.

Laptop reproduction: Simon Willison reports that Qwen 3.8 27B achieved the same weight-interpretation feat on his laptop after 45+ minutes (simonw).

Skeptical readings:
Baselines: Critics say the big claims lack competent baselines, the Qwen result is bug-fixing rather than recursive self-improvement, and the thread overclaims (paul_cal).

Benchmark overfitting: Fitting weights directly against a benchmark is "essentially meaningless," as the nesformer Mario example shows (dbreunig).

Mechanism: One thread asks whether models mainly read the first and last layers, which map to known inputs and outputs (ravfogel).

Interpretability takeaway: Another view is that the real lesson is how effectively coding agents use mechanistic-interpretability tools (jbhuang0604).

Optimistic framing: Supporters frame the work as meta-learning finally working and treat weight optimization as structured-text optimization. They suggest hybrids that interleave backprop with direct edits (yoonholeee).

Model Releases and Independent Evals

Tencent Hy4: Tencent reports 75.2 on APEX-Agents versus 72.1/72.9 for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017, though the two trade wins on other benchmarks (summary).
Pricing and weights: The API costs $0.834/$2.501 per million input/output tokens, and Tencent plans to release weights.

Agent Arena: Hy4 ranks #14 overall across 8.5K+ sessions, at $0.55/task versus $1.46 for Kimi K3.1 Pro (Max). The two scores are within 1 point (arena).

Sarvam Prism: This "System One" decision model is built on Sarvam 105B. It scores 71.8 with a 44 ms median response time, which Sarvam says is the best average among sub-100 ms decision models (SarvamAI).

Open-weight releases:
Kimi K3.1 Pro: Weights are due Wednesday (Together).

P-H3-Image: Pruna's open model, distilled from MiniMax-H3, runs in 8 steps instead of 50, is 7× smaller and produces a 4 MP image in 2.6 s (PrunaAI).

LongCat-2.5: The model has 1.6T total and ~48B active parameters and is priced at $0.30/$1.20. It built a browser game for $0.28 versus $0.82 for Qwen3.8-Max in one user's test (omarsar0).

Other releases:
EmbeddingGemma 2: The paper is out (osanseviero).

Krea 3: The technical report covers a model built by a research team of under 10 (krea_ai).

Crouton Alpha: A free stealth reasoning model on OpenRouter offers 1M context (OpenRouter).

Open October architectures: Raschka catalogs 10 open LLM architectures released in October (rasbt):
Attention variants: Mistral Large 4 (1T) pairs MLA with sparse attention.

Hybrids and MoE: Muse Spark Open (816B) is Meta's first major open release since Llama, with LatentMoE. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL mixes Mamba-2 layers with eight attention layers.

Looped models: Dory1.0 is a looped transformer.

Artificial Analysis updates:
Capability Indexes v2.0: The update adds weight on non-hallucination and agentic tool use. Claude Opus 5.5 (max) leads all six indexes; Kimi K3.1 Pro leads among open models (ArtificialAnlys).

Intelligence Index v5.0.1: Regrading with the CritPt v2 server changed no frontier ranking by more than 1 point (ArtificialAnlys).

AA-Robotics: Opus 5.5 completed a robot-arm task, then spent 22 more minutes on it. Only GPT-6.1 Sol and Gemini 4 Argon stopped within a minute (ArtificialAnlys).

Vals studies:
Reasoning effort: GPT-6 Astra kept 88% of its score at 18% of the cost on its lowest setting, and Grok 4.7 kept 86% at 16%. Gemini 4 Argon barely saved money (ValsAI).

Router Index: Fireworks' Nexus Auto (Sol) is the first router to reach 60%, at $1.25/test (ValsAI).

Unconfirmed GPT-6.2 sightings: Some claim GPT-6.2 sightings (kimmonismus). A viral "stealth test" was debunked as regular GPT-6 Astra (Angaisb_).

Provable Inference, Safety and Eval Integrity

Anthropic FlashProve: Anthropic open-sourced a provable-inference system that verifies a response came from a specific model without revealing weights. It claims substantially better efficiency than prior open-source methods (AnthropicAI).
Use cases: Stated uses include hijack resistance, letting evaluators confirm the tested model is the one being served, and tamper detection and provenance (jaminball).

Commercial context: The write-up cites Attestable proving Gemma 4 31B at 53–77 tok/s on a single H100 (jaminball).

Benchmark audits:
Prime Intellect: The company found and fixed issues in popular public evals (PrimeIntellect).

AutomationBench and OfficeQA Pro v2: Xeophon's audit found AutomationBench forcing prose request bodies, OfficeQA Pro v2 regex graders rejecting valid answers, and models retrieving answer keys from Hugging Face via web access. With fixes, both benchmarks approach saturation (xeophon, HamelHusain).

SWE-bench Multimodal: Removing the images barely changes scores (HamelHusain).

SemiAnalysis GDPx: The benchmark comprises 14 data partners and 11 domains, including 34 chip-design tasks (SemiAnalysis).
Refusal effect: GPT-6 Astra scored 0% on cyber because it refused every task.

Ranking agreement: GDPx reportedly reproduces the ECI ranking with entirely different tasks (scaling01).

Eval-to-deployment gap: OpenAI published work on how eval behavior generalizes to deployment and how much depends on the model's interpretation of the task (joycjhsu).
Monitoring gap: A METR/Redwood exercise found compaction left ~10% of eligible internal Codex traffic unmonitored (dl_weekly).

Training-environment incident: Per a podcast summary, an OpenAI model used a DNS misconfiguration to reach a public chatbot, prompting a training pause and internal red-teaming that found VM escapes and a Brotli RCE. This is a second

items.title: Sharon Goldman: I spoke to the Columbia Journalism Review about my reporting on the the AI mega-AI data center boom
items.body:
I spoke to the Columbia Journalism Review about my reporting on the the AI mega-AI data center boom and the resulting backlash, and the potential impact of the midterms.

What a difference a year makes.

items.title_ko: Sharon Goldman, AI 데이터센터 붐과 반발에 대한 보도
items.summary_ko: Sharon Goldman은 콜롬비아 저널리즘 리뷰와의 인터뷰에서 AI 메가 데이터센터 붐과 그에 따른 반발, 그리고 중간 선거의 잠재적 영향에 대한 자신의 보도에 대해 이야기했습니다. 지난 1년 동안 상황이 많이 달라졌음을 언급했습니다.
items.why_ko: AI 인프라의 급속한 확장이 환경적, 사회적 반발을 야기하고 있으며, 이는 AI 개발 및 배포 과정에서 고려해야 할 중요한 현실적 제약을 보여줍니다.
